title: Called up in 1941 and taking his trumpet to the reception center
summary: Back at the dance hall, drafted, and playing trumpet on the train and at the reception center.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And then, 41, I went back to work a few weeks, a few months or so, at the foreign dance hall, the same dance hall, see. Well, then Uncle Sam called me there, and I had to go in army. Well, after Uncle Sam called me in army, I went in army. I took my trumpet with me when I got in army. A lot of fellas told me, I need to take that trumpet away. He said, man, we can have some fun. So I took the trumpet. And all on the train I was playing the trumpet, you know. And after I played the trumpet with the lieutenant, the fellas gave me a lot of privilege that I didn't usually get, you know. Let me get off the train. Once the soldiers get off, I'm going to get off the train and talk to people, you know. And when I went there, and I got in army at the reception center, I used to take my trumpet. Well, those numbers were very popular then. This heart of mine, this love of mine, this love of mine, you made me love, you know. Well, I got around the area and started blowing the trumpet, you see. Well, the lieutenants and the fellas around there got busy, they didn't want me to leave the camp, see. They didn't want me to stay there. It was impossible, see, when the soldiers got there, they got to carry you out, they got the trumpet, you know. But they did keep me there. All those fellas I came there with, I used to stand up there and blow up my butt and all that, you know, and say those blues things, they actually go for the lead.
